meta.title: FROTH-RFC-0005: Legible Follow and Execution Log Reader
meta.status: PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED; core reader now landed in CLI and FollowLive
meta.author: Charlie (@charliebuddybot)

section.title: Situation
section.p: Froth now has a growing execution surface:

item.p: agent cycles
LLM requests and streamed edits
tool lifecycles
Telegram bot/runtime activity
background tasks
provider and transport telemetry

section.p: The raw data exists, but the operator experience is still rough.
Today there are two main readers:
Both work, but both are still very close to the raw event stream.
mix froth.follow currently prints:

item.p: raw event name
optional duration
flat metadata key/value pairs

section.p: That is useful for debugging internals, but not for following a run. It forces the human reader to do projection work in their head:

item.p: which cycle or span matters?
which events are noise and which are milestones?
which start/stop pair belongs together?
which tool failure actually changed the outcome?
which lines are operator-relevant versus transport chatter?

section.p: TelemetryLive has the same problem in a different shape. It is a generic table of raw events, not a focused execution-log reader. It truncates details, has no real semantic grouping, and does not yet feel like the UI version of follow.

RFC-0004 points in the right direction: Froth needs an execution spine, not just transcripts plus raw telemetry. But even before that full persistence model lands, the project already needs a much better way to read what is happening.
The immediate opportunity is strong:

item.p: RFC-0003 now emits explicit agent.tool.* lifecycle events
spans and parent IDs already exist
telemetry_events already gives us durable history
a future agent_events expansion is coming in RFC-0004

section.p: The missing piece is a presentation model.

section.title: Goal
section.p: Make Froth's live and historical execution traces readable by humans.
Concretely:

item.p: mix froth.follow should become the best way to watch a cycle run
a future LiveView should feel like the same reader in a richer UI
raw telemetry should remain available, but not be the default view
formatting logic should be shared, not duplicated between CLI and UI

section.title: Current Status
section.p: As of 2026-03-24, the core reader described here is in place, but the surrounding navigation and drill-down work is still incomplete.

item.p: Froth.Follow.Entry, Froth.Follow.Projector, and Froth.Follow.Renderer exist
Froth.Follow.Source now exists as the shared recent-history loader for follow readers
mix froth.follow now renders projected follow entries instead of formatting raw telemetry inline, boots with recent matching history, and supports smart/raw/errors plus cycle/span filtering
mix froth.follow now starts only the local repo state it needs, uses unique telemetry handler IDs, and no longer crashes when projected entries omit optional detail

the shared projector now treats froth.agent.control.outcome as a first-class semantic family, so yields, reply-sent, tool-error, and cycle-error outcomes render as operator-facing rows instead of raw metadata blobs
the agent runtime now emits live froth.agent.control.outcome telemetry, so control outcomes appear while tailing instead of only after a page reload
smart mode now suppresses duplicate persisted execution-spine tool rows while keeping raw mode as the exact escape hatch
FollowLive now exists as a dedicated execution-log reader with Smart, Raw, and Errors modes, historical boot, live append, search, cycle/span pinning, and inline payload expansion
TelemetryLive still consumes the same projected entry model, so the shared semantic layer remains real rather than duplicated
projector behavior is covered by focused tests, including control-outcome and renderer regression coverage, and the LiveView has integration coverage for smart/raw/errors rendering

section.p: That means the shared semantic layer is no longer hypothetical.
What is still not done:

item.p: richer durable navigation state for cycle/span/task pinning, including saved views and task-level deep links
richer filtering beyond text plus first-pass cycle/span scope filters
a richer raw detail pane with linked navigation instead of a simple inline payload expansion
deeper task/message-aware pinning instead of the current cycle/span-only scope controls
a more complete preference strategy for typed execution-spine rows over inferred telemetry across all duplicated families, not just the first-pass tool-row suppression now in smart mode
This RFC does not replace raw telemetry storage.
This RFC does not require RFC-0004's schema changes first.
This RFC does not propose persisting every token delta in a UI feed.
This RFC is not a redesign of the generic Telemetry page into a universal observability suite.

section.title: Thesis
section.p: Froth should stop rendering raw telemetry directly and instead render projected follow entries.
The right layering is:

item.p: collect raw runtime events from telemetry and later agent_events
project them into a stable semantic Follow.Entry
render those entries differently in CLI and LiveView

section.p: The shared projection layer is the key. Without it:

item.p: mix froth.follow gets one set of heuristics
the LiveView gets a different set of heuristics
the same event means different things in different readers
future event-log work in RFC-0004 has no stable consumer model

section.p: With it:

item.p: formatting gets better once and benefits both readers
the app can mix live telemetry with persisted event rows
the same execution vocabulary can power search, filtering, grouping, and UI navigation

subsection.title: 1. Raw event names are too low-level
subsection.p: This:
is mechanically correct but cognitively noisy.
Operators usually want:
plus a small number of relevant details.

subsection.title: 2. Metadata is unprioritized
subsection.p: Current output gives every metadata field the same visual weight. Important fields like:
get mixed together with lower-value plumbing fields.

subsection.title: 3. There is no semantic grouping
subsection.p: The current readers do not really understand:

item.p: span trees
cycle boundaries
think/tool alternation
task lifecycle
error severity

subsection.p: So humans have to infer the shape of the run from a firehose.

subsection.title: 4. CLI and LiveView would currently drift
subsection.p: If we improve only mix froth.follow, the web reader will stay raw. If we improve only the LiveView, the terminal reader stays second-rate. The shared model should come first.

subsection.title: 1. Introduce a shared projection layer
subsection.p: Add a Froth.Follow namespace with modules along these lines:
Froth.Follow.Entry should represent a human-facing event row, not a raw telemetry tuple. Example fields:
The important shift is that summary and detail are already projected for human reading.

subsection.title: 2. Project raw events into semantic families
subsection.p: Raw event names should map into a smaller semantic vocabulary.
Example families:
Example projections:

item.p: froth.agent.cycle.start -> cycle started
froth.agent.cycle.stop with structured outcome yield -> cycle yielded
froth.agent.cycle.stop with structured outcome assistant_stopped_without_reply -> cycle stopped without reply
froth.agent.tool.started -> tool <name> started
froth.agent.tool.completed -> tool <name> completed
froth.agent.tool.failed -> tool <name> failed
froth.agent.tool.timed_out -> tool <name> timed out
froth.agent.control.reply_sent -> reply sent
froth.tasks.completed -> task <id> completed
froth.http.sse.text_delta -> hidden in smart mode, visible in raw mode

subsection.p: The point is not to lose the raw event. The point is to provide a semantic default.

subsection.title: 3. Make "smart mode" the default for follow
subsection.p: mix froth.follow should default to a smart view, not raw telemetry.
Smart mode should:

item.p: collapse noisy transport events
highlight boundaries and failures
prefer semantic summaries over raw metadata dumps
keep stable columns so the eye can scan quickly

subsection.p: Suggested modes:

item.p: smart default operator view
raw exact telemetry view
errors only warnings/failures/timeouts

subsection.title: 4. Give entries stable visual slots
subsection.p: Each rendered line should have a predictable shape:
For example:
subsection.code: 14:58:01.123 cycle 01J... cycle started model=claude-opus-4-6 14:58:01.456 think thinking started 14:58:02.091 tool echo froth_echo started call=toolu_... 14:58:02.119 tool echo froth_echo completed 28ms result=text 14:58:02.403 llm response completed 311ms in=842 out=119 14:58:02.418 tool shell run_shell timed out 30000ms 14:58:02.420 cycle 01J... cycle failed tool timed out after 30000ms
subsection.p: This is much easier to read than the current "event name plus bag of keys" style.

subsection.title: 5. Separate primary detail from raw detail
subsection.p: Each projected entry should expose:

item.p: a primary summary for fast scanning
a small detail string for top-priority fields
the full raw event for drill-down

subsection.p: In CLI smart mode, show summary + small detail. In CLI raw mode, show the whole raw payload. In LiveView, show summary by default and raw JSON in a side panel or expandable drawer.

subsection.title: 6. Correlate by cycle and span by default
subsection.p: Follow readers should understand correlation, not just printing order.
Important scope identifiers:
The shared projector should normalize those IDs and surface them in a consistent place. That lets both CLI and UI offer:

item.p: follow one cycle
filter to one span subtree
jump from a tool failure to related events
show only entries related to a given task or message

subsection.title: 6.5. Make control outcomes first-class in the reader
subsection.p: The follow reader should not infer control flow from transcript text.

A recent concrete bug made this obvious: a transcript tool returned a code snippet containing the string Yielding: and the runtime treated that text as a real yield signal. The CLI and LiveView should not repeat that mistake at the presentation layer.
Instead, the projector should prefer explicit runtime outcomes such as:
Those outcomes should render as distinct summaries, for example:
subsection.code: 15:05:30.842 control reply sent chat=-1003690254489 15:05:34.339 tool transcript read_tool_transcript done 111ms 15:05:34.460 cycle 01K... cycle yielded waiting on subscribed task 15:05:34.461 cycle 01K... stopped without reply assistant requested tool and ended
subsection.p: The point is not just better wording. It is to make the reader report what the runtime actually decided, not what a human might guess from nearby text.

subsection.title: 7. Build the LiveView on the same entries
subsection.p: The future LiveView should not be another generic telemetry table. It should be a real execution-log reader.
Suggested structure:

item.p: left rail for high-level filters and saved scopes
center timeline of projected follow entries
right detail pane for raw JSON, spans, and linked records

subsection.p: Important UI behaviors:

item.p: stream new entries live
pin to a cycle/span/tool/task
pause/resume live updates
toggle smart/raw view
expand a row into raw event payload
group or fold uninteresting transport chatter
deep-link by cycle ID or span ID

subsection.p: This can begin on top of telemetry_events and later incorporate RFC-0004's richer agent_events without changing the UI model.

subsection.title: 8. Keep raw telemetry as an escape hatch
subsection.p: The system should never trap operators in a projected view.
Both readers should keep a raw mode because:

item.p: projector bugs happen
new event types will arrive before they are beautifully formatted
debugging sometimes needs the exact payload

subsection.p: The rule should be:

item.p: smart mode for default readability
raw mode for exact truth

subsection.title: 9. Design for mixed live and historical sources
subsection.p: The same follow entry model should be usable with:

item.p: live telemetry attached through :telemetry.attach_many
persisted rows from telemetry_events
future typed rows from agent_events

subsection.p: That means the projection API should accept either:

item.p: raw telemetry tuples
persisted telemetry rows
future execution-log rows

subsection.p: This is important because the LiveView will want both:

item.p: a historical bootstrapped timeline
live appended updates
extract formatting logic out of Mix.Tasks.Froth.Follow
define Follow.Entry
implement smart/raw rendering
add semantic projections for current high-value families: - agent - control - tool - llm - tasks - telegram
make smart mode the default
add --raw
add --errors
add filters by cycle/span/prefix
improve duration and summary formatting
stream projected entries in a LiveView
support historical boot plus live append
add row expansion for raw payload
add cycle/span pinning and text filtering

subsection.title: Phase 4: Integrate RFC-0004 data
subsection.p: As agent_events becomes a real execution log, the projector should start preferring typed execution events over inferred raw telemetry where possible.

section.title: Why This Should Happen Before A Bigger UI Rewrite
section.p: The follow/output problem is mostly not a CSS problem. It is a semantic projection problem.
If Froth jumps straight to a fancy LiveView without first defining the shared event-entry model, it will only create a prettier version of the same raw unreadability.
The projector layer is the leverage point.

section.title: Recommendation
section.p: Do this in the following order:

item.p: extract a shared follow projection layer
make mix froth.follow excellent in smart mode
build FollowLive on that same projected entry stream
connect the same reader to RFC-0004's future execution log

section.p: That creates one coherent operator experience across terminal, web, live telemetry, and persisted history.
